newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas falls to five-month low.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas falls to five-month low.

text.p: Gasoline prices on Tuesday dipped to a five-month low amid high stocks and an abundance of sellers.
"Inventories are very high...almost at tank tops," said a trader with a major oil company.
Singapore fob cargoes of 50,000-barrels lifting end April/early May were offered at $24.80 per barrel by a European major for 95-octane unleaded, and $25.10 by a Dutch trader for 97-octane unleaded.
On Monday, the 95-octane unleaded grade was offered at $25.00.
The last time prices were at $24.80 was in early November last year.
A U.S. major also had some 95-octane unleaded barrels from Yanbu for end-April delivery.

Traders said the Yanbu cargo which normally trades at a premium of 30 cents per barrel c-and-f over Singapore quotes, was offered at flat while buying interest was only heard at a discount of 50 cents.
"It is not finalised...we may not have anything," said the major. "We have to make sure we supply our affiliate."
The weak gasoline market has also started to depress prices for high aromatic naphtha (HAN) used for reformate production.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp State-owned Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) lastest HAN tender which closed on April 10, only managed to attract low bids.

The 25,000 tonnes of HAN lifting April 21-25 was awarded to Dutch trader Vitol at $32.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob Bombay on the west coast, much lower than the last award at a $25.00 discount for a cargo lifting March 10-12.
IOC meanwhile has two more HAN cargoes to sell by tender - 28,000 tonnes lifting April 25-27 from Madras on the east coast and 20,000 tonnes lifting April 30-May 2 from Cochin on the west coast.
Both tenders close on April 17 and bids will be valid for one day.

IOC's last HAN tender from Madras, lifting March 27-29, was awarded at $22.28 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis while its Cochin HAN tender, lifting April 1-3, was awarded at $19.08.

In comparison, low aromatic naphtha (LAN) however fetched a better premium with IOC's tender for 27,000 tonnes of LAN lifting April 21-25 to Swiss trader Glencore at $19.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob Madras.
The tender closed on April 10 and was valid for one day.

IOC's last LAN tender from the east coast, lifting Vizag during mid-April, was awarded at $25 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on an fob basis, while its last Madras LAN cargo, lifting January 27-29, was awarded at a $23-to-$24 discount.
Naphtha swaps firmed slightly to $21.70/$21.85 per barrel from $21.60/$21.80 on Monday.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
